subject: Proxy chunked header decoding failure — ClearWave production impact
messages:
From: Katherine Moore <katie@clearwave.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T14:12:00Z
Subject: Production errors when using Redwood client behind EdgeProxy

Hi Jonas —

We're seeing a sharp rise in 5xx errors and streaming disconnects from our production service after we upgraded to Redwood Client 1.8 and put the traffic through EdgeProxy (v2.4). Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~8% starting ~08:45 PDT on Nov 1. Errors appear during large prompt streams; clients get an immediate connection close and there are "proto: invalid header" style traces in our sidecar logs.

Sample failure cluster: attached error_log_20261101.txt (snippets of stack traces, request ids). This is customer-facing — sessions drop and revenue is impacted. Can you please triage urgently? We're open to temporary workarounds (roll back to 1.7, force non-chunked streaming, proxy config changes) but need a recommended path and ETA for a fix.

Thanks,
Katherine Moore
Head of Platform
ClearWave AI

Subject: Re: Production errors when using Redwood client behind EdgeProxy — initial triage

Triage notes (quick):
- Reproduced locally with EdgeProxy reproducer config. Root cause appears to be the SDK streaming parser's strict handling of chunked-transfer-encoding metadata. EdgeProxy is inserting an extra pseudo-header when doing TLS termination for streamed responses; our parser expects a single contiguous header block and fails when the header is split across chunk boundaries. That mismatch leads to an immediate framing error and connection close.

Stack excerpt (sanitized):
- parser.go:214: decodeChunkHeader() -> panic: unexpected CRLF position
- stream.go:88: handleChunk() -> ErrInvalidHeader

Attachments: sdk_dump_20261101.tar.gz (contains reproducer + core dumps), included small sdk_trace.json snippet inside the archive.

Proposed near-term mitigation (hours):
1) Relax header parsing to accept header fragments across chunks (hotfix patch).
2) Add fallback to aggregate the first N bytes before parsing.
3) Provide client config flag to disable chunked streaming (non-chunked fallback) for ClearWave as a stop-gap.

I'll prepare a canary build for us to push to a small percentage of traffic. Laura/Marissa: please prep customer comms offering a short-term config change and informing them we will push a targeted fix.

— Dev

Update: hotfix deployed to canary (us-west-2 small pool) at 2026-11-02T22:45Z. The patch relaxes header parsing and implements the first-byte aggregation fallback. Canary results:
- Error rate dropped from 8% -> 0.7% for canary traffic within 90 minutes.
- No new regressions observed in p95 latency.

Next steps:
1) Extend canary to 25% for the next 6 hours, monitor for regressions.
2) If stable, schedule full rollout during a short maintenance window (we have approval for emergency change, per Avery).
3) Postmortem and follow-up ticket created: INFRA-2145 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-2145).

Marissa/Laura: suggested customer note: explain root cause (header fragmentation + proxy rewrite), outline immediate mitigations (canary hotfix + config flag for non-chunked), and timeline for full rollout (target: 2026-11-04 morning). Offer goodwill credit pending SLA review.

Attachments: canary_metrics_S1.png (snapshot showing error rate improvement).
